newsitem.title: UK: Enterprise Oil off, Merrill Lynch dowgrades.
newsitem.headline: Enterprise Oil off, Merrill Lynch dowgrades.

text.p: Shares in Enterprise Oil Plc fell on Monday as analysts at Merrill Lynch said they had downgraded their recommendation on the stock to "reduce" from "neutral".
The shares were seven pence weaker at 667-1/2 by 1045 GMT.

Merrill Lynch analyst Jonathan Wright said there were four main factors behind the downgrade -- weakening oil prices, the stock's high premium to net asset value (NAV), waning bid speculation and an absence of opportunities to add to its NAV in the short term through drilling.

"We are concerned the stock has over-reached itself and may be due a correction," Wright said. He said the share price could correct to around 600p but this would be a gradual process rather than a sharp drop.
"We've been expecting a correction in oil prices for a while and that's looking more likely as inventories start to build as we enter the spring," Wright said.
"Also, Enterprise is at around a 45 percent premium to NAV. That looks quite excessive and already there's a lot of expectation in the share price," he said.

"In the absence of a bid the upside looks very limited and as time drags on, if there are no more bids, then that speculation may start to wane, and the whole sector may move down as a result," he added.
Wright said most of Enterprise's high-potential acreage would yield longer-term results. "In the short term at least, Enterprise may have trouble adding to its NAV through drilling," he said.
Wright said LASMO Plc would be the most attractive stock in the sector to switch into. He said Merrill Lynch had re-iterated an "accumulate" recommendation on the stock.
"It looks less stretched on valuation and we think there's quite a substantial chance it can add substantially to NAV in the near term," he said.
